setup.name: Two-group espresso machine
setup.note: Nuova Simonelli Appia Life Compact two-group volumetric, 110V: $7,600.00 at WebstaurantStore, usually ships in 2-4 weeks. Price before sales tax, delivery and installation. D03: 120 months assumes a technician visit every 6-12 months and working water treatment; about 72 months without care. Basis: a service company states that a maintenance schedule stretches a machine from 5-7 years to 10-15 (vendor claim, beanandbrewtech.com), and a US repair shop does not normally take machines 10 or more years old because repair then costs over half of a new one (1st-line.com). No independent service-life statistic was found. Tax life is shorter: IRS 5-year property. Maker warranties run about 12-13 months and are void without certified installation and water treatment (seen in La Marzocco dealer terms).

setup.name: Espresso grinder
setup.note: Mahlkonig E65S grind-by-time: $2,099 at Visions Espresso (listed as discontinued and out of stock on the day I looked; its successor E65W is $3,099). Lifespan is my estimate. D03: no service-life figure for the grinder body was found, so 72 months stays an estimate. The wear part is the burr set: Mahlkonig rates the E65S 65 mm steel burrs at about 800 kg of coffee and sells the set for $149.99 (mahlkoenig.us). At the reference 6,000 orders a month, with about 70% of orders taking a 20 g dose (my assumption), the shop grinds 84 kg a month: new burrs every 9-10 months. With one grinder, a dead motor stops every espresso drink.

setup.name: Second grinder for decaf
setup.note: A second Mahlkonig E65S at the same $2,099 seen at Visions Espresso. D03: at decaf volume (about a tenth of the espresso orders, my assumption) the 800 kg burr set outlives the grinder. Its real value is as a spare: when the main grinder fails, espresso keeps flowing.

setup.name: Water filtration for the espresso machine
setup.note: Research notes allowance for a filter head, cartridge and fittings; listed there: Everpure ESO7 cartridge $192.94, QL2 head $41.94. Cartridges are replaced several times a year (in the maintenance line). D03 correction: cartridge life is set by gallons and hardness, not by the calendar. Pentair's spec sheet rates the Everpure ESO 7 at 5,300 grains: 600 gallons at 150 ppm, at no more than 0.5 gallons a minute, replaced when the volume is reached or at least once a year. New York City water averages about 1.8 grains per gallon (DEP), so one cartridge treats about 2,900 gallons; where Croton water is blended in, hardness can reach 7 grains and the same cartridge lasts about 760 gallons. At roughly 20 gallons a day through the espresso machine and brewer (my assumption) that is about 5 months on soft water and 5-6 weeks on the hardest.

setup.name: Under-counter milk fridge and reach-in refrigerator
setup.note: Avantco A-19R-HC 29-inch reach-in refrigerator $1,199.00 (seen at WebstaurantStore) + Atosa MGF8401GR under-counter refrigerator $1,429 (from research notes; the dealer page refused my request). D03: 120 months is the typical life the Department of Energy took for commercial refrigeration, as reported by the trade press; the same article says units that are not maintained often serve only 6-8 years, and dealer guides give 10-15 years with care, 8-10 in hard use. A compressor replacement is quoted at about $1,800-$2,800, more than either of these units costs new, so a dead compressor here means a new fridge (the usual rule: replace when the repair passes 50% of a new unit). Avantco's warranty is 1-3 years of parts and labor depending on the series, 5 years on the compressor for eligible units, commercial installation only.

setup.name: Refrigerated pastry display case
setup.note: Avantco BCS-48-HC 48-inch refrigerated countertop bakery case: $1,149.00 at WebstaurantStore. Larger floor cases run to $9,800. D03: same class as the fridges: about 10 years with clean coils, 6-8 without (trade press on the Department of Energy assumption).

setup.name: Ice machine
setup.note: Research notes allowance next to a clearance Manitowoc UYF0140A at $3,479.40; the 2026 list price of the current model is $6,392. Without it you buy bagged ice for iced drinks. D03: dealers give 7-10 years with regular cleaning and filter changes (KaTom, GoFoodservice); 8.5 years taken. A dealer blog gives 4-5 years for a neglected machine. Makers call for cleaning and sanitizing about every 6 months; the FDA Food Code leaves the interval to the manufacturer. Average repair call for an ice machine: $708.41 in 2021 (FER magazine). Renting instead costs about $155-$250 a month with cleaning, repairs and backup ice included.

setup.name: Under-counter commercial dishwasher
setup.note: Noble Warewashing HT-UC24 high-temperature under-counter dishwasher with booster heater: $4,449.00 at WebstaurantStore. Not mandatory: washing by hand in the three-compartment sink (wash, rinse, sanitize) is legal. D03: undercounter warewashers last 5-10 years with proper maintenance (FE&S); 7.5 years taken; a trade magazine gives 10-15 years for a well-built, well-kept unit. Health Code §81.29: a machine that sanitizes with hot water must bring the dish surface to at least 160°F and carry thermometers; a chemical (low-temperature) machine needs a test kit, and a kit that is missing or unused is a $200 violation (code 10G). Hand washing in the three-compartment sink needs 170°F water for 30 seconds or a chemical sanitizer.

setup.name: POS register, receipt printer and cash drawer
setup.note: Research notes: Square Register $899 (Square's store, 2026) plus $400 allowance for a printer, cash drawer and mounts. D03: Square's own page lists the Register at $899 before taxes (or $44 a month over 24 months), the Terminal at $299 on the hardware page and $399 on the home page, the Stand at $149. The 48-month lifespan stays an estimate; the IRS treats a cash register as 5-year property (asset class 57.0).

setup.name: Lidded bins, fire extinguisher, CPR kit, safety signs, alarm
setup.note: Research notes allowance. Seen on the NYC Business restaurant page: restaurants must keep one adult and one pediatric resuscitation mask and two pairs of gloves. D03: every portable extinguisher must carry the FDNY tag; a W-96 certificate holder from an FDNY-approved company services it at least once a year and replaces the tag, and the owner names someone to do a monthly quick check recorded on the back of the tag (FDNY). A shop that only warms food needs no Class K extinguisher; one with cooking equipment does.

setup.name: Used two-group espresso machine (refurbished)
setup.note: A US dealer's 2026 guide puts a used two-group La Marzocco Linea Classic at $5,000-$8,000; single listings seen in search results: $4,900 used and $8,500 refurbished (2017 build), against $12,730-$16,480 new. $6,500 is the middle of the guide's range. Dealer warranties on used machines are 1-3 months of parts, against 12-13 months on a new one. 60 months of remaining life is my assumption: half of a 10-year service life. Have a technician open the boiler and look for scale before you pay.

setup.name: Upgrade to a dual-boiler specialty espresso machine
setup.note: A new two-group La Marzocco Linea Classic S was listed at $12,730 at one US retailer and $16,480 at another (search results, November 2026); the upgrade costs the difference from the $7,600 compact machine = $5,130. 144 months: the upper half of the 10-15 years a service company gives for a maintained machine. New machines carry a 13-month parts and labor warranty that requires installation by a factory-certified technician and water treatment. The quality bonus is a game value.

setup.name: Used milk fridge and reach-in refrigerator
setup.note: Dealer and auction guides: buyers pay 30-70% less than new for used restaurant equipment, while sellers get only 10-30% of the original price. Half of this pack's $2,628 pair is taken. No warranty. 48 months of remaining life is my assumption (a 10-year unit bought at year 6). Older units may run on R-404A, a refrigerant that is being phased down, so a leak can cost more than the fridge.

setup.name: Certified installation of the espresso machine
setup.note: Three hours at $250, the on-site hourly rate on the price page of a New York City espresso service company (one-hour minimum, then billed by the quarter hour; established service departments elsewhere publish $130-$135 regular and $260 emergency). Covers the water line, drain, power hookup and calibration. Dealers void the warranty on a machine that was not installed by a certified technician with water treatment in place. Check the voltage first: a 240V heating element gives only about 75% of its power on a 208V building supply.

setup.name: Commercial blender with sound enclosure
setup.note: Vitamix The Quiet One: $1,158.05 at KaTom (list $2,708.89); Prima Coffee lists it at $1,424.99. Vitamix warranty: 3 years on motor base parts, 1 year labor, 1 year on the container and blade assembly. No service-life figure was found: 60 months is the IRS recovery period for restaurant and retail equipment. The quality bonus is a game value.

setup.name: Hot water dispenser for tea and americanos
setup.note: Bunn H5X 5-gallon, 120V, 1,850W: $1,087.00 at WebstaurantStore (the black version is $989.00). It takes the hot-water load off the espresso machine boiler at the morning peak. No service-life figure was found: 108 months is the IRS class life for retail and restaurant equipment (asset class 57.0, 9 years). It scales like any boiler: descale on the schedule.

setup.name: Undercounter freezer
setup.note: Avantco AU-27F 27-inch undercounter freezer: $1,199.00 at WebstaurantStore (the 48-inch AU-48F is $1,399.00). Needed for frozen pastry dough and ice cream drinks. Lifespan as for the fridges: about 10 years with clean coils.

setup.name: Countertop convection oven for baking off pastry
setup.note: Avantco CO-16 half-size countertop convection oven, 120V, 1,600W: $389.99 at WebstaurantStore. Bakes frozen croissants and cookies on site. No service-life figure was found: 60 months is the IRS recovery period. The quality bonus is a game value. Ask your architect whether the menu needs an exhaust hood: anything that makes grease smoke does.

setup.name: Panini grill
setup.note: Avantco PG100, 120V, 1,750W: $179.99 at WebstaurantStore; the larger PG200GST with a timer is $348.49. A 1,750W appliance needs its own 15-amp circuit. 60 months is the IRS recovery period; no service-life figure was found.

setup.name: Commercial microwave
setup.note: Solwave 1,000W commercial microwave: $235.00 at WebstaurantStore (Amana $310.00, Panasonic NE-1064F $630.00). 60 months is the IRS recovery period; no service-life figure was found.

setup.name: Ventless high-speed oven for hot sandwiches
setup.note: Pratica Fit Express, 208/240V single phase, 6,200-7,000W: $10,540.33 at WebstaurantStore. It heats a sandwich in under a minute without a hood, but FDNY approval is given model by model: ask the dealer for the Fire Department Certificate of Approval before you buy. It needs a dedicated 208/240V circuit. 108 months is the IRS class life; no service-life figure was found. The quality bonus is a game value.

setup.name: Two-tap cold brew and nitro dispenser
setup.note: Kegco two-tap commercial cold brew dispenser: $1,637.37 (sale price). Simpler two-faucet units start at $939.99-$999.99 (Keg Outlet); a Micro Matic commercial unit is $5,103.00. It is a refrigerator: same 10-year life with clean coils. New York State fire code permits apply to carbon dioxide systems above 100 lb; a small nitrogen cylinder is below that, but ask the gas supplier. The quality bonus is a game value.

setup.name: Wireless temperature sensors for the fridges
setup.note: Three sensors at $28.99 and one hub at $39.99 = $126.96 (MOCREO list prices seen in search results; the basic cloud plan is free). Professional kits cost far more: a single Kitchen Brains sensor is about $182. The sensors text you when a fridge warms up overnight; they go blind if the Wi-Fi or power is out. 60 months is the IRS recovery period.

setup.name: Second, battery-powered card terminal
setup.note: Square Terminal: $299 on Square's hardware page (or $27 a month over 12 months); the home page showed $399 on the same day, so check the price at checkout. A second device keeps cards working when the register dies and can take payments offline.

setup.name: Replacement air conditioner (3-5 ton unit, installed)
setup.note: Not an opening purchase when the space comes with working air conditioning: this is what replacement costs when the old unit dies. A New York City contractor price page quotes $5,000-$12,000 installed for a 3-5 ton rooftop unit (indicative only); $8,500 is the middle. A crane lift adds $1,500 or more, and rooftop work needs Buildings Department permits. ASHRAE's median service life for rooftop air conditioners is 15 years. Most leases make the tenant maintain and replace the unit that serves only its space: read the clause and ask the unit's age before signing.

setup.name: Replacement water heater (30-50 gallon tank, installed)
setup.note: Not an opening purchase when the space has a working heater. Replacement in New York: $2,400-$3,500 for a 50-gallon tank (HomeBlue, 2022) and $2,200-$4,400 on a 2026 plumber price page that adds a $280 Buildings Department permit and a $130 inspection; $3,300 is the middle. Tank water heaters last 8-12 years (ASHRAE figure for gas tank heaters); 10 taken. Without hot water at the hand sink you cannot legally serve.

setup.name: Scale inspection for selling beans by weight
setup.agency: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
setup.note: NYC311: the city inspects every scale used to sell goods by weight once a year and bills $20 for a scale up to 33 lb ($40 up to 660 lb); a scale that passes gets an official seal, and a scale that fails may not be used. After a request you get the inspection date within 15 days. Only needed if you weigh beans at the counter; pre-packed bags with a printed net weight need no scale.

monthlyCosts.name: Small repairs: bulbs, door hardware, gaskets, fittings
monthlyCosts.note: D03 correction: the old $300 line bundled everything. It is now itemized below: grease interceptor pump-out, repair calls, backflow test, extinguisher service, burrs, cleaning chemicals and smallwares, while filter cartridges and preventive service are levers. What is left here is a $45 allowance for bulbs, door closers, fridge gaskets and fittings (my allowance, no public figure). All maintenance lines together come to about $480 a month before the levers, against $300 before.

monthlyCosts.name: Grease interceptor pump-out
monthlyCosts.note: $75 a month is the saving this pack already gives for skipping the pump-out (shortcut skip_grease_trap_cleaning); it is taken out of the old maintenance line so the two agree. A New York cost guide lists commercial grease trap cleaning at $300-$800 a visit: about one visit every 4-10 months at this rate. The rule: grease may not fill more than 25% of the interceptor.

monthlyCosts.name: Repair calls: plumbing, refrigeration, espresso, air conditioning
monthlyCosts.note: Three service calls a year x $754.10, the average restaurant service request in 2024 (86 Repairs) = $2,262 a year = $189 a month. The number of calls is my planning assumption: no public statistic of repair calls per small cafe was found. By equipment (86 Repairs, 2021): reach-in refrigerator $519.05, plumbing $666.28, air conditioning $1,019.90; a technician on site costs $135 before any work. These are repairs that happen even with good care; breakdowns from skipped maintenance come on top.

monthlyCosts.name: Yearly backflow preventer test
monthlyCosts.note: City rule (15 RCNY §20-04, DEP): each backflow prevention assembly is tested at least once a year by a state-certified tester employed by a licensed master plumber, at the customer's expense, and the report is filed with DEP. No New York City price was found: $450 a year is taken from the $389-$559 quoted for New Rochelle (an upstate utility charges $100 per device) = $38 a month. Applies when DEP requires a device on your water service; DEP mails a letter when the test is due.

monthlyCosts.name: Yearly fire extinguisher service and FDNY tags
monthlyCosts.note: FDNY: every extinguisher carries the FDNY tag and is serviced at least once a year by a W-96 certificate holder from an approved company. Price from one New York vendor list: $15-$25 per unit for 1-10 extinguishers plus a $50-$150 trip fee: 3 units x $20 + $100 = $160 a year = $13 a month.

monthlyCosts.name: Grinder burrs
monthlyCosts.note: Mahlkonig: E65S burr set $149.99, rated for about 800 kg. With 70% of orders taking a 20 g dose (my assumption) an order uses 0.014 kg: $149.99 / 800 x 0.014 = $0.0026 per order, about $16 a month at 6,000 orders. Dull burrs grind slower and hotter and the coffee tastes flat.

monthlyCosts.name: Espresso machine, grinder and brewer cleaners
monthlyCosts.note: Backflush powder: Urnex Cafiza 20 oz $9.69 (WebstaurantStore), about one jar a month at 16 g a day; grinder cleaner: Urnex Grindz $25.99 (urnex.com), one jar per quarter = $8.70; descaler for the brewer: Dezcal 1 liter $15.99 per quarter = $5.30. Total about $24 a month. Usage is my estimate from the dosing on the labels.

monthlyCosts.name: Broken and lost smallwares
monthlyCosts.note: This pack's own figures: $2,000 of pitchers, cups, tampers, scales and bins with a 24-month life = $83 a month. It was part of the old maintenance line.

shortcuts.name: Keep the milk after a warm night
shortcuts.what: The fridge failed or the power was out, and the milk sat above 41°F for more than 2 hours. The rule says throw it out; keeping it saves about $50 a month on average. Warm or spoiled food is a public health hazard: $250-$600 and 7 to 28 points.

shortcuts.name: Skip the yearly backflow test
shortcuts.what: The valve that keeps your espresso machine, ice machine and dishwasher water from flowing back into the city main must be tested every year by a certified tester. Skipping it saves about $38 a month. The city knows who has not filed: fines start at $700.

shortcuts.name: Let the fire extinguisher tags expire
shortcuts.what: Every extinguisher needs a yearly service and a fresh FDNY tag. Skipping it saves about $13 a month. A fire inspector who finds an expired or missing tag writes a summons: $600, or $300 if you fix it and admit it.

shortcuts.name: Let a handyman plumb and wire new equipment
shortcuts.what: A licensed plumber or electrician with a Buildings Department permit costs about $125 a month more over a year of installs and replacements. Work without a permit costs 21 times the permit fee, at least $6,000, even if you rip it out afterwards.

shortcuts.name: Keep a failing fridge in service
shortcuts.what: The reach-in no longer holds 41°F on hot afternoons. Putting off a new one saves about $219 a month. Equipment that cannot keep food cold is a critical violation, $300-$350, and the warm milk in it is a second one.

shortcuts.name: Stay open with a dead water heater
shortcuts.what: The heater died and a replacement with a permit takes days. Staying open on cold water saves about $275 a month. A hand sink without hot water is a critical violation, $300-$350, and the inspector can close you until it runs hot.

shortcuts.name: Drain the ice machine into a bucket
shortcuts.what: A proper drain line with an air gap means a plumber. Letting the ice machine and the fridge drip into a bucket saves about $56 a month. Inspectors cite it as improper drainage, and standing water breeds drain flies.

violations.name: Not enough working refrigeration to keep food cold
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.18; 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 05F
violations.note: Penalty schedule as quoted by the search tool from the codified appendix and a Health Department notice: code 05F, hot or cold holding equipment not provided or inadequate (§81.18), $300 and $350, a critical violation. The food in the warm unit is cited separately under 02G ($250-$600, 7-28 points). The climb from $325 to $350 is a game formula.

violations.name: Hand wash sink without hot and cold running water
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.21(a), §81.21(b); 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 05D
violations.note: Seen in the penalty schedule notice: 05D, "Hand wash facility without hot and cold running water or water at inadequate pressure", §81.21(a) and (b), critical; $300 and $350 for 05D in a 2023 notice. "No hot and cold running water or water at inadequate pressure" appears among the violations of restaurants the Department ordered closed (weekly closure lists). The Department closes a place when a public health hazard cannot be corrected before the inspection ends; one day of closure is a game value.

violations.name: Equipment not properly drained; no backflow protection
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.20; 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-B, code 10B
violations.note: Code 10B text seen: "back-siphonage or back-flow prevention device not provided where required; equipment or floor not properly drained; sewage disposal system in disrepair"; the scoring guide gives a refrigerator draining condensation into a bucket and an air conditioner draining onto the sidewalk as examples. A general violation: 2 to 5 points. The dollar amount for 10B was not seen; $200 is the amount seen for another general violation (10G), so this is an estimate.

violations.name: No accurate thermometer in a refrigerator
violations.law: 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-B, code 10E; NYC Health Code §81.18
violations.note: Code 10E text seen: "Accurate thermometer not provided or not properly located in refrigerated or hot holding equipment", counted per unit. A separate critical code, 04J, covers a missing probe thermometer for food: $200-$300. The dollar amount for 10E was not seen; $200 is the amount seen for general violation 10G, so this is an estimate.

violations.name: Backflow preventer not tested this year
violations.law: 15 RCNY §20-04 (NYC Department of Environmental Protection, backflow prevention)
violations.note: Rule seen: each assembly is tested at least once a year by a state-certified tester employed by a licensed master plumber; failure to provide the annual test report is a violation that leads to a summons; defects are repaired within 30 days. Amounts: "not less than $700 nor more than $10,000" civil, $1,400-$10,000 criminal, quoted by the search tool from a City Council file (Int 0768-2026) on these penalties; I could not tell from the excerpt whether that is the current or the proposed range, hence an estimate. The monthly climb is a game formula.

violations.name: Fire extinguisher missing or without a current FDNY tag
violations.law: NYC Fire Code §906; 3 RCNY §109-03, violation category 1 (portable fire extinguishers)
violations.note: FDNY summons schedule, violation category 1 "Portable Fire Extinguishers and Fire Hoses" (OATH code BF01): the figures 600, 300, 1,000 and 1,500, 750, 5,000 were quoted by the search tool; read as penalty, mitigated penalty and maximum for a first violation, then the same three for repeats. The column reading is mine, hence an estimate. FDNY guide: violations are issued for extinguishers without a proper tag.

violations.name: Plumbing, gas or electrical work without a permit
violations.note: Seen in the Administrative Code: for a building other than a one- or two-family home the penalty is 21 times the permit fee, never less than $6,000 nor more than $15,000; removing the work does not avoid it. Electrical violations issued after December 21, 2025 are calculated the same way (Buildings Department service notice). A permit must still be obtained afterwards.

officials.name: Health inspector
officials.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
officials.realProcess: Unannounced, at least once a year. The inspector walks the whole shop with a thermometer and a flashlight and scores each violation in points: under 14 is an A. With 14 or more, a second inspection comes at least 7 days later and sets the grade. Fines are decided afterwards at a city hearing (OATH).
officials.d03: correction: four equipment violations added to checks

officials.name: Water and sewer inspector
officials.realProcess: Inspectors visit food businesses, open the grease interceptor, measure how full it is and ask for cleaning records. The same department tracks every backflow preventer: it mails a letter when the yearly test is due and issues a summons when no report arrives.

officials.name: Fire inspector
officials.agency: New York City Fire Department (FDNY), Bureau of Fire Prevention
officials.realProcess: Fire Prevention inspectors come for permit inspections and complaints. At every visit they check that each extinguisher carries a current FDNY tag and, where there is cooking, that the hood cleaning decal and the suppression system service are in date.

officials.name: Buildings inspector
officials.realProcess: Inspectors answer 311 complaints about construction, plumbing, gas or electrical work done without a permit. They can issue a violation with a civil penalty and a Stop Work Order; the penalty is due even if the work is removed.

reports.name: Report no hot water or warm fridges (311)
reports.text: The Health Department sends an inspector to check the hand sinks and the fridge thermometers. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report work without a permit (311)
reports.text: The Buildings Department checks whether the plumbing, gas or electrical work has a permit. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report a fire safety problem (311)
reports.text: The Fire Department checks the extinguishers and their tags. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

events.name: Card payments down for a day
events.text: Your payment company has an outage. Registers freeze or run offline, and shops across the city go cash-only for the day.
events.note: Real case: Square was down for most of a day on September 7-8, 2023; shops went cash-only. Game effect: one day of 30, with half of card customers walking away (90% pay by card): 1/30 x 0.9 x 0.5 = 1.5% of the month. The walk-away share is my estimate.

events.name: Water main break on your block
events.text: A main bursts under the street. The water is off until the city repairs it, and no water means no coffee and no hand washing.
events.note: Seen in the Mayor's Management Report: 552 water main breaks in fiscal 2025, the most since fiscal 2015 (7.9 per 100 miles of main). Game effect: one day closed out of 30 = 3.3%. The one-day duration is my estimate.

events.name: Planned water shut-off for street work
events.text: The city posts a notice: water off from morning until the end of the workday. You have 24 hours to fill containers or plan a short day.
events.note: Seen at the Department of Design and Construction: notices are posted at least 24 hours ahead, water goes off in the morning and is back by the end of the workday. Game effect: half a day of 30 = 1.5%.

events.name: Power failure in your Con Edison network
events.text: A feeder fails and the block goes dark for the afternoon. The register runs on battery; the fridges do not.
events.note: Seen in Con Edison's 2025 annual reliability report: in the underground network system 16.6 interruptions per 1,000 customers a year, lasting 6.70 hours on average; in the overhead system 439 per 1,000 and 2.02 hours. Game effect: half a day of sales = 1.5% of the month; spoiled stock is extra (see extra.mechanics).

events.name: Internet down across the neighborhood
events.text: A cut cable takes the internet out for most of a day. Shops without a backup line or offline mode cannot take cards.
events.note: Real cases: vandals cut a Spectrum fiber line in Queens in 2017, 60,000 customers were out for more than 15 hours and card sales stopped; Verizon Fios was down about 4 hours on November 12, 2024. Game effect for a shop with offline mode: 1% of the month.

events.name: Heat wave: fridges and ice machines fall behind
events.text: A week above 90°F. Compressors run without rest, ice machines cannot keep up, Con Edison lowers the voltage, and every technician in the city is booked.
events.note: Real cases: Con Edison cut voltage by 8% in parts of Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx in August 2022 (about 252,000 customers) and reduced voltage in Brooklyn and Staten Island in June 2025. Service calls for refrigeration and ice machines peak every June, July and August. The 3% loss of serving capacity is my estimate; staffAvailability is used because the engine has no equipment capacity target yet.

ruleCards.title: Fridges must hold 41°F
ruleCards.text: Cold food must stay at 41°F or below. A fridge that cannot hold it is a critical violation, $300-$350; the warm milk inside is a second one, $250-$600 and 7 to 28 points. Replace the fridge before the inspector does it for you.

ruleCards.title: No hot water, no service
ruleCards.text: Every hand wash sink needs hot and cold running water. Without it: a critical violation, $300-$350, and the Health Department can close the shop until the water runs hot. A dead water heater is an emergency, not a repair for next week.

ruleCards.title: Drains and air gaps
ruleCards.text: Ice machines, fridges and air conditioners must drain into a proper drain, not a bucket or the sidewalk, and water lines need backflow protection. Inspectors cite it under code 10B: 2 to 5 points each time.

ruleCards.title: A thermometer in every fridge
ruleCards.text: Each refrigerator needs an accurate thermometer in its warmest part (code 10E), and the shop needs a probe thermometer for food: without one the fine is $200-$300. A $10 thermometer is the cheapest insurance in the shop.

ruleCards.title: Backflow test every year
ruleCards.text: If your water service has a backflow preventer, a state-certified tester working for a licensed master plumber must test it every year and file the report with DEP. No report means a summons: fines run from $700 to $10,000.

ruleCards.title: Fire extinguisher tags
ruleCards.text: Every extinguisher needs an FDNY tag renewed each year by an approved company, plus a monthly check you record on the back of the tag. A missing or expired tag: $600, or $300 if you fix it and admit it, up to $1,000 if you ignore the summons.

ruleCards.title: Permits for plumbing, gas and electrical work
ruleCards.text: New water lines, gas piping and electrical circuits need a licensed trade and a Buildings Department permit. Work without one costs 21 times the permit fee: at least $6,000, at most $15,000, even if you remove the work.

ruleCards.title: The 2-hour rule
ruleCards.text: When the power or a fridge fails, keep the doors shut. Cold food that stayed above 41°F for less than 2 hours may be chilled again and sold. More than 2 hours, or you do not know how long: throw it out.

ruleCards.title: Tell the Health Department
ruleCards.text: After a fire, flood or power outage that may have left food above 41°F, the owner must notify the Health Department immediately (Health Code §81.43). The Department can order service stopped while the hazard lasts.

ruleCards.title: Con Edison pays for spoiled stock, sometimes
ruleCards.text: If a failure in Con Edison's local network leaves you dark for more than 12 hours in 24, a business can claim up to $12,900 of spoiled perishables. File within 30 days with an itemized list and proof. Storm outages are not covered.

ruleCards.title: After 72 hours without power
ruleCards.text: State law: when a widespread outage lasts 72 hours or more, the utility must reimburse small businesses for food spoiled by lack of refrigeration. You need an itemized list and proof of loss within 14 days. Photograph everything before you throw it out.

ruleCards.title: Cards without internet
ruleCards.text: A Square register can take cards offline, but the payments must upload within 72 hours and you carry the loss if a card is later declined. Set a per-sale limit, and never log out or reset the device before it reconnects.

ruleCards.title: Your water depends on your block
ruleCards.text: New York City water averages 1.8 grains of hardness per gallon, very soft. Where Croton water is blended in it can reach 7 grains: the same softening cartridge then lasts a quarter as long. Ask DEP which supply feeds your address.

ruleCards.title: What voids the warranty
ruleCards.text: Espresso machine warranties last about 12-13 months and exclude scale and bad water. Most are void unless a certified technician installed the machine with water treatment. Keep the install invoice and the filter change log.

ruleCards.title: Ice is food
ruleCards.text: Makers ask for an ice machine to be cleaned and sanitized about every 6 months. Mold or slime inside is a dirty food-contact surface: a critical violation, $200-$300 and 5 to 8 points. A neglected machine lasts 4-5 years instead of 7-10.

ruleCards.title: Sanitizing dishes
ruleCards.text: By hand: wash, rinse, then sanitize in 170°F water for 30 seconds or in a chemical solution. A dish machine must reach 160°F at the dish surface or use a chemical sanitizer with a test kit: no kit, or an unused one, is a $200 violation.

ruleCards.title: Selling beans by weight
ruleCards.text: A scale used to sell goods by weight must be inspected and sealed by the city every year: $20 for a scale up to 33 lb. A scale that fails may not be used. Pre-packed bags with a printed net weight need no scale.

ruleCards.title: Equipment and taxes
ruleCards.text: Equipment is not lost money on your tax return: under Section 179 a business can deduct the full cost in the year it starts using it, up to $2,560,000 in 2026. Without that choice it is written off over 5 years.

ruleCards.title: Leasing a machine
ruleCards.text: A leased espresso machine costs about $217 a month per $10,000 at 11% over 5 years, and New York sales tax of 8.875% is due on each payment. Most leases need a personal guarantee: the payments continue if the shop closes.

ruleCards.title: Con Edison pays for upgrades
ruleCards.text: Con Edison's small business program covers up to 70% of the cost of efficient lighting, refrigeration and controls for customers under 300 kW. Apply first: work started before the offer letter does not qualify.

ruleCards.title: Used equipment
ruleCards.text: Used restaurant equipment sells 30-70% below new, with a warranty of 0 to 3 months. When you sell it yourself you get 10-30% of what you paid. Buy used from a closing cafe; never count on equipment to get your money back.

ruleCards.title: When the gas is locked
ruleCards.text: After a leak the utility shuts the gas and will not restore it until a licensed plumber repairs the piping, the Buildings Department signs off and the lines pass a pressure test. New York restaurants have waited 2 to 7 months. All-electric shops are spared.

ruleCards.title: Water shut-offs
ruleCards.text: For planned street work the city posts notices at least 24 hours ahead: water goes off in the morning and returns by the end of the workday. A main break comes with no notice: the city had 552 of them in fiscal 2025.

ruleCards.title: The free espresso machine
ruleCards.text: A roaster may lend or discount the machine if you buy its coffee: typically 20-40 lb a week. The rent is built into the bean price. Fall below the minimum or leave early and the machine is no longer free. Read the exit terms.

roadmap.title: Have inherited equipment tested before you sign
roadmap.text: Ask the age of the air conditioner, the water heater and every fridge left in the space, and who must replace them under the lease. Pay a technician for an hour to open the espresso machine and look for scale: $250 now against $7,600 later.

roadmap.title: Check the water and the voltage at the address
roadmap.text: Ask DEP which water supply feeds the block: soft water needs a softening cartridge every 5 months, blended Croton water every 5-6 weeks. Ask the electrician whether the building supplies 208 or 240 volts before you order the machine.

roadmap.title: Book a certified installer for the espresso machine
roadmap.text: The warranty holds only if a certified technician installs the machine with water treatment. Budget about three hours at $250. Keep the invoice.

roadmap.title: Line up your repair people before you open
roadmap.text: Find an espresso technician, a refrigeration and air conditioning company, a licensed plumber and an electrician now. Write their numbers, your model numbers and the weekend rates on one sheet by the register. A Saturday breakdown is too late to start looking.

roadmap.title: Backflow preventer test and fire extinguisher tags
roadmap.text: Have the backflow preventer on your water line tested by a certified tester and the report filed with DEP. Have an FDNY-approved company service and tag every extinguisher. Both repeat every year.

roadmap.title: Optional: scale inspection for selling beans by weight
roadmap.text: If you weigh beans at the counter, request a city scale inspection. You get a date within 15 days; the fee is $20 a year for a scale up to 33 lb.

roadmap.title: Ask Con Edison to pay part of your efficient equipment
roadmap.text: Con Edison's small business program covers up to 70% of efficient lighting, refrigeration and controls. Apply and wait for the offer letter before the work starts, or it does not count.

roadmap.title: Prepare for a day without power, water or cards
roadmap.text: Turn on the register's offline mode and set a per-sale limit. Keep a cash float and a cash-only sign. Put a thermometer in every fridge. Know the 2-hour rule for cold food, and where the water shut-off valve is.

suppliers.what: Installation, preventive maintenance, emergency repair and loaner machines
suppliers.whereToFind: Your roaster first: most wholesale programs include or arrange service. Then independent espresso technicians: ask the cafes around you who answers on a Saturday. Compare the hourly rate, the minimum charge, the weekend rate and whether they stock parts for your brand.

Names are sources of prices, not endorsements.

suppliers.what: Coil cleaning, gaskets, refrigerant leaks, ice machine cleaning, seasonal tune-ups
suppliers.whereToFind: Commercial refrigeration and HVAC companies that serve restaurants; ask for a maintenance plan with a set number of visits. Technicians who handle refrigerant must hold a federal certification.
suppliers.examples: Local commercial refrigeration contractors; national repair networks used by restaurants
suppliers.note: Average repair calls in restaurants (86 Repairs, 2021): reach-in refrigerator $519.05, walk-in cooler $1,000.42, air conditioning $1,019.90. Call volume peaks in June, July and August: book the tune-up 8-10 weeks before the first heat wave (facilities company advice).

suppliers.what: Water lines and drains for equipment, water heater replacement, yearly backflow test, drain cleaning
suppliers.whereToFind: Licensed master plumbers: check the license on the Buildings Department website. The backflow tester must be state-certified and work for a licensed master plumber.

A cafe owner on a coffee forum paid $175 to clear a line packed with coffee grounds.

suppliers.what: Yearly service and FDNY tags; hood cleaning and suppression service if you cook
suppliers.whereToFind: Only companies approved by the Fire Department, with a certificate holder (W-96 for extinguishers, W-64 or P-64 for hood cleaning). Ask for the certificate number.
suppliers.note: One New York price page lists $15-$25 per extinguisher for 1-10 units, plus a $50-$150 trip fee (a lead-generation style site: indicative only).

suppliers.what: A rented ice machine with cleaning, repairs and backup ice included
suppliers.whereToFind: Ice machine subscription companies and local refrigeration dealers. Compare the monthly price with a machine you own plus two professional cleanings a year.
suppliers.note: About $155-$250 a month for a cafe-size machine; a setup fee applies. Name from search results, not an endorsement.

suppliers.what: Lease-to-own with a $1 buyout, or a loan, for the espresso machine and refrigeration
suppliers.whereToFind: The dealer's finance partner, your bank, or an equipment finance company. Ask for the annual rate, not a factor; ask about the personal guarantee and what happens if you close.
suppliers.examples: Dealer financing, equipment finance companies, lease marketplaces
suppliers.note: Rates seen in 2026 guides: about 11% for good credit, 6-18% overall, terms of 24-84 months. Two-group machines are listed for lease from $78 to $248 a month (Kwipped). New York sales tax is due on each lease payment.

suppliers.what: A machine lent, discounted or financed by your coffee roaster, with training and service
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask each roaster you consider what it offers a new wholesale account: equipment, installation, maintenance, training. Get the weekly minimum, the price per pound and the exit terms in writing.
suppliers.examples: Counter Culture Coffee, Stumptown Coffee Roasters, Joe Coffee Company
suppliers.note: Seen on roaster pages: installation, calibration, scheduled maintenance and responsive service (Counter Culture); 24/7 equipment help (Stumptown); technical support and equipment solutions (Joe Coffee). None publishes prices or minimums. A buying guide puts typical minimums at 20-40 lb a week or $300-$600 of coffee a week.

suppliers.what: A cellular line that takes over when the cable or fiber drops, so cards keep working
suppliers.whereToFind: Your mobile carrier or your internet provider; ask for automatic failover.
suppliers.examples: Business backup plans from the large carriers
suppliers.note: $30-$35 a month before equipment and fees. Reference outages: Verizon Fios, about 4 hours across the East Coast on November 12, 2024; Spectrum in Queens, more than 15 hours for 60,000 customers in 2017.

conditionalMonthlyCosts.name: Hood cleaning and suppression system service
conditionalMonthlyCosts.appliesIf: The shop cooks under an exhaust hood (not the base cafe)
conditionalMonthlyCosts.note: FDNY: exhaust systems are cleaned every 3 months or as often as needed by a certified company with a Fire Department decal, and the suppression system is serviced at least every 6 months by a licensed contractor. No price was found: amount left at 0 on purpose.

eventCatalog.name: Scale kills the heating element
eventCatalog.text: The espresso machine trips the breaker and will not heat. The technician finds the element caked in limescale.

cause.when: water_treatment is yearly or none until untreated hardness passes 13,000 grains: none on soft water 12 months, yearly on soft water 20 months, none or yearly on Croton-blend water 3-4 months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Hardness of the water at the address (DEP: 1.8 grains per gallon on average, up to 7 where Croton water is blended) x gallons through the machine since the last working cartridge
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Scale from poor water is described as the number one cause of commercial espresso machine failure (facilities company Vixxo); no failure rate is published.
eventCatalog.note: Cost: heating element work $240-$520 (repair shop price page) taken at $380 + two hours on site at $250 (the price page of one New York City service company) = $880. The repair price page is a lead-generation style site: indicative only. Downtime 3 days without a service plan (visit plus part), 1 day with a plan and loaner: my estimates. Sales lost: espresso drinks, 65% of orders (assumption), drip coffee keeps selling if there is a batch brewer. Timing: 20 gallons a day x 1.8 grains = 1,080 grains a month untreated; x 7 grains = 4,200 a month; tolerance 13,000 grains is a game parameter.

eventCatalog.name: Group gaskets harden and leak
eventCatalog.text: Portafilters no longer lock tight and water sprays around the basket. Shots run uneven and the bar is wet all day.

cause.when: espresso_service is none for 6 months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Months since gaskets, shower screens and baskets were last changed
eventCatalog.realFrequency: A parts maker calls quarterly replacement of gasket, screen and basket the bare minimum of preventive maintenance.
eventCatalog.note: Cost if a technician is called: one hour at $250 + a $30 kit. With the in-house routine the kit alone is $20-$40 a quarter. The quality loss is a game value.

eventCatalog.name: Pump or control board fails on an old machine
eventCatalog.text: No pressure at the group, or the display goes blank. The machine is past its best years.

cause.when: machine age passes its neglected lifespan (72 months) without a service plan, or a used machine reaches the end of its remaining life (60 months)

eventCatalog.realSignal: Age of the machine in months against lifespanMonths
eventCatalog.realFrequency: A US repair shop does not normally repair machines 10 or more years old: repair usually exceeds 50% of a new machine.
eventCatalog.note: Repair shop price page: pump $220-$680, control board $380-$550; middle $450 + two hours at $250 = $950. After the lifespan the same bill returns every 6 months until the machine is replaced: my game rule.

eventCatalog.name: It breaks on Saturday morning
eventCatalog.text: The machine dies at 7 a.m. on Saturday. Your technician answers on Monday.

cause.when: any espresso machine failure while espresso_service is not contract: add two days of downtime and the emergency rate

eventCatalog.realSignal: Day of the week of the failure; whether a service plan with weekend response exists
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Service contracts are often quoted as next working day, Monday to Friday; published emergency rates are double the regular rate ($260 against $130 an hour at one service company).
eventCatalog.note: Two weekend days without espresso: 2/30 x 65% = 4.3% of the month, more in a shop where weekends are the best days. Emergency labor: two hours at $260. An insurance blog describes exactly this case: a Saturday breakdown, a technician on Monday, a full day of revenue gone.

eventCatalog.name: Warranty claim denied
eventCatalog.text: The machine fails in its first year. The dealer asks for the installation invoice and the filter log, and you have neither.

cause.when: a failure in the first 12 months when espresso_install was skipped or water_treatment is none

eventCatalog.realSignal: Warranty terms: certified installation and water within specification
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Makers and dealers list water damage, poor water quality and scaling as exclusions; one maker calls water outside specification the most common reason for machine failure.
eventCatalog.note: The owner pays the repair that the warranty would have covered: $880 as in espresso_scale_failure. New machine warranty: 12-13 months (La Marzocco dealer terms).

eventCatalog.name: The used machine was full of scale
eventCatalog.text: Three months in, the bargain machine stops heating. The 3-month parts warranty ended last week.

cause.when: espresso_machine_used bought without the roadmap step check_inherited_equipment: failure in month 4

eventCatalog.realSignal: Whether a technician inspected the boiler before purchase
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Used dealer warranties run 1-3 months of parts, against 12-13 months on a new machine.
eventCatalog.note: Game rule: an uninspected used machine carries the previous owner's scale. Cost as in espresso_scale_failure.

eventCatalog.name: Dull burrs
eventCatalog.text: Shots take longer to grind and taste flat. Nobody has counted the kilos since opening.

cause.when: espresso_service is none for 10 months: nobody tracks the 800 kg burr life

eventCatalog.realSignal: Kilograms ground since the last burr change against the 800 kg rating
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Mahlkonig rates the E65S burrs at about 800 kg at a medium setting: 9-10 months at 84 kg a month.
eventCatalog.note: Burr set $149.99. The quality and speed losses are game values.

eventCatalog.name: The only grinder dies
eventCatalog.text: The grinder motor hums and stops. Without ground coffee the espresso machine is furniture.

cause.when: grinder age passes 72 months, with no second grinder

eventCatalog.realSignal: Age of the grinder; number of grinders owned
eventCatalog.realFrequency: No failure statistic found; a coffee program has four points of failure: water, machine, grinder, people (facilities company).
eventCatalog.note: With a second grinder nothing is lost: move the hopper. Repair: two hours at $250. The 72-month grinder life is the pack estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Harder water in the mains
eventCatalog.text: The city is sending more Croton reservoir water into the system. Tap water tastes different and carries up to four times the minerals.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DEP announcements of increased Croton supply; hardness at the address (1.8 grains per gallon average, up to 7 in blended areas)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: DEP raised the Croton share for two weeks in March 2023 and for about three weeks from October 16, 2023; the Delaware Aqueduct shutdown planned from October 1, 2024 was to last up to eight months.
eventCatalog.note: Filter life: 1.8 / 7 = 0.26 of normal. A shop that changes cartridges by the meter pays about four times as much for those weeks ($152 instead of $39 a month); a shop on a yearly schedule takes the scale. Which blocks get the blend is not published by address: ask DEP.

eventCatalog.name: Brown water after work on the main
eventCatalog.text: Hydrant flushing or main repairs stir up sediment. The tap runs brown for a while.
eventCatalog.realSignal: 311 discolored water reports; DEP hydrant and water main work on the block
eventCatalog.realFrequency: DEP: street construction or water main work can cause discolored water; run the cold tap until it is clear (15-30 minutes in shut-off notices).
eventCatalog.note: Stop brewing for about an hour and change the cartridge early: $192.94 (pack price). The lost hour is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Compressor burns out in July
eventCatalog.text: The reach-in is warm when you open. The condenser coil is a felt blanket of dust and the compressor is dead.

cause.when: refrigeration_care is none: the fridge fails at half its life (60 months; a used fridge in its first July)

eventCatalog.realSignal: Months since the condenser coils were cleaned; outdoor temperature
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Trade guides: a dust-clogged coil can halve compressor life; dirty coils are a primary cause of compressor failure. Refrigeration was 16.6% of restaurant service requests in 2021 (86 Repairs).
eventCatalog.note: A compressor replacement ($1,800-$2,800) costs more than this pack's fridges, so the unit is replaced: $1,199 + $600 of spoiled dairy and pastry (assumption) = $1,800. One day of improvised service from coolers: 30% of sales lost that day is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: The fridge was warm all night
eventCatalog.text: A torn door gasket, a door left ajar, a tripped breaker. At 6 a.m. the milk reads 52°F and nobody knows since when.

cause.when: refrigeration_care is none for 12 months, or after any power outage, while temperature_checks is not sensors

eventCatalog.realSignal: Fridge temperature log; time above 41°F
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Equipment monitoring vendors note that cooler failures typically happen after closing; a chain operator put one freezer or walk-in failure at $15,000-$20,000 of stock (a much larger kitchen).
eventCatalog.note: Rule: above 41°F for more than 2 hours, or for an unknown time, means discard. Stock on hand $600 (assumption). With sensors the alert comes at night and the stock is moved in time.

eventCatalog.name: Slime in the ice machine
eventCatalog.text: The inspector opens the ice machine and wipes a finger along the inside. It comes out pink.

cause.when: refrigeration_care is none for 6 months and an inspection happens

eventCatalog.realSignal: Months since the ice machine was cleaned and sanitized
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Makers call for cleaning about every 6 months, more often where yeast is in the air; the Food Code leaves the interval to the manufacturer.
eventCatalog.note: Cited as a dirty food-contact surface: this pack's dirty_surfaces violation, $200-$300 and 5 to 8 points. The reputation loss is a game value.

eventCatalog.name: No ice in a heat wave
eventCatalog.text: The ice machine quits on the hottest day of the year. Half the orders today are iced.

cause.when: refrigeration_care is none during the announced heat wave

eventCatalog.realSignal: Days above 90°F; months since the ice machine was serviced
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Service calls for ice and refrigeration equipment peak every June, July and August; a Houston restaurant reported its ice machine going down about six times in one heat wave.
eventCatalog.note: Repair $708.41 (average ice machine call, 2021) + bagged ice runs for three days (about $90: my estimate from $2.59-$5.99 per 20 lb bag at retail). Staff time on ice runs costs half the iced orders: 3/30 x 50% x 50% = 2.5% of the month. A subscription includes backup ice.

eventCatalog.name: Refrigerant gets scarce
eventCatalog.text: The federal phasedown of older refrigerants tightens supply. Recharging an old fridge now costs more than the fridge is worth.
eventCatalog.realSignal: EPA HFC allowance schedule (30% of baseline from 2029); wholesale refrigerant prices
eventCatalog.realFrequency: EPA's own analysis projects refrigerant prices 12-24% higher by 2029 (as cited by the contractors' association ACCA). In New York a court temporarily blocked the state ban on R-404A on March 27, 2026.
eventCatalog.note: 18% is the middle of the 12-24% range. It hits used and inherited units that still run on R-404A; new self-contained units use R-290.

eventCatalog.name: Every technician is booked
eventCatalog.text: In a heat wave every kitchen in the city calls for refrigeration service in the same week. Without a plan you wait.
eventCatalog.realSignal: National Weather Service heat advisories for New York City

effects.scope: any refrigeration, ice or air conditioning failure this month without a service plan

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Facilities companies: call volume on refrigeration and ice equipment spikes every June, July and August; do preventive service 8-10 weeks before the first heat wave.
eventCatalog.note: The two extra days are my estimate; emergency labor is billed at about double the regular rate.

eventCatalog.name: The water heater leaks
eventCatalog.text: A puddle under the tank and cold water at the hand sink. No hot water means no legal service.

cause.when: the inherited heater passes 120 months and was not replaced; its age is revealed by the roadmap step check_inherited_equipment

eventCatalog.realSignal: Age of the water heater on its data plate
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Tank water heaters last 8-12 years (ASHRAE figure for gas tank heaters).
eventCatalog.note: Replacement $2,200-$4,400 with a permit; two days closed is my estimate for a licensed plumber with a permit. "No hot and cold running water" is among the violations of restaurants the Health Department closed.

eventCatalog.name: Bar sink backs up
eventCatalog.text: Months of coffee grounds and milk fat have set in the drain line. The bar sink fills and will not empty.

cause.when: cleaning is minimal for 6 months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Whether grounds go into a knock box or down the sink; months since the drain line was cleaned
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Plumbing was more than a quarter of restaurant service requests in 2021, $666.28 a call on average (86 Repairs).
eventCatalog.note: A cafe owner on a coffee forum paid $175 to clear a line packed with grounds; New York pages list $300-$500 for a main line and $400-$1,000 after hours; $400 taken.

eventCatalog.name: Drain flies
eventCatalog.text: Small flies hover over the floor drain and the bucket under the ice machine. An inspector who sees one looks harder at everything.

cause.when: shortcut drain_into_bucket or cleaning minimal for 2 months in warm months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Standing water and organic film in drains
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Pest control companies: drain flies breed in the organic buildup of uncleaned drains; coffee grounds feed them.
eventCatalog.note: Leads to this pack's pest_activity violation at the next inspection. The reputation loss is a game value.

eventCatalog.name: DEP letter: backflow test due
eventCatalog.text: The Department of Environmental Protection reminds you that the yearly test of your backflow preventer is due.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Twelve months since the last test report was filed
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every year for every device; DEP mails a notification letter when the test is due.
eventCatalog.note: A reminder event: it makes the shortcut visible at the right moment.

eventCatalog.name: Air conditioning fails in a heat wave
eventCatalog.text: It is 96°F outside and 88°F at the counter. Guests take their iced coffee and leave; the fridges struggle in the hot room.

cause.when: hvac_service is none during the announced heat wave; if the unit is older than 180 months it must be replaced

eventCatalog.realSignal: Days above 90°F; months since the last tune-up; age of the unit
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Air conditioning had the highest average repair cost of any restaurant equipment in 2021: $1,019.90 (86 Repairs). In July 2026 a Connecticut donut shop closed early when its air conditioning gave out overnight in the heat.
eventCatalog.note: Three days at 30% fewer sales (my estimate for a room nobody wants to sit in). Replacement instead of repair: $5,000-$12,000 installed plus crane. In 2026 the owner of an East Harlem restaurant kept the air conditioning off through summer days in the 90s after the gas and electric bill reached $1,400 a month (Bloomberg, October 2026).

eventCatalog.name: The air conditioner drips
eventCatalog.text: The condensate line is clogged. Water runs down the wall, onto the sidewalk and through the ceiling tile above table four.

cause.when: hvac_service is none for 12 months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Months since the condensate drain was cleared
eventCatalog.realFrequency: The inspection guide lists an air conditioner draining onto the sidewalk as an example of improper drainage (code 10B).
eventCatalog.note: One visit: $135 on-site fee + one hour at $130. Cited under this fragment's improper_drainage violation if an inspector sees it first.

eventCatalog.name: No heat in a cold snap
eventCatalog.text: The same rooftop unit that cools the room heats it, and it will not start. Guests keep their coats on and do not stay.

cause.when: hvac_service is none during an announced cold snap

eventCatalog.realSignal: Days below 20°F; months since the last tune-up
eventCatalog.realFrequency: No heating-specific statistic found; the repair cost is the 2021 air conditioning average.
eventCatalog.note: Commercial tenants usually heat their own space; check the lease. The 30% loss on two days is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: The block loses power for the afternoon
eventCatalog.text: A feeder cable fails. Lights, grinder, espresso machine and fridges stop; the register runs on its battery.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison outage map for the network that feeds the block
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Con Edison, 2025: 16.6 interruptions per 1,000 customers a year in the underground network system, 6.70 hours on average; 439 per 1,000 and 2.02 hours in the overhead system. On July 13, 2019 about 72,000 customers on the West Side of Manhattan were dark for about five hours.
eventCatalog.note: Half a day of sales. A 6.7-hour outage is under the 12 hours Con Edison requires for a spoilage claim, and over the 2 hours after which warm food must go: keep the fridge doors shut. The owner must notify the Health Department (§81.43).

eventCatalog.name: More than 12 hours without power
eventCatalog.text: The repair runs into the next day. Everything in the fridges is lost.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison estimated restoration time; whether the cause is its own equipment or a storm
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Rare in the network system: the average interruption there is 6.70 hours.
eventCatalog.note: Con Edison pays a business up to $12,900 for perishables spoiled when a failure of its local distribution system lasts more than 12 hours in 24: file within 30 days with an itemized list and proof of loss. Nothing is paid when a storm caused the outage. Stock on hand $600 (assumption): the claim returns it in full if the player files.

eventCatalog.name: Storm: three days dark
eventCatalog.text: A coastal storm takes down power across the borough. Crews say days, not hours.
eventCatalog.realSignal: National Weather Service tropical storm and wind warnings; Con Edison storm outage counts
eventCatalog.realFrequency: No frequency found. The state law on prolonged outages (Public Service Law §73) was written for this case.
eventCatalog.note: Con Edison's own claim rule excludes storms. State law (Public Service Law §73) steps in after 72 consecutive hours of a widespread outage: small businesses are reimbursed for spoiled food with an itemized list and proof within 14 days. Utility-interruption insurance pays lost income after its waiting period (24 hours in one policy example). The cap for small businesses was not seen.

eventCatalog.name: Con Edison lowers the voltage by 8%
eventCatalog.text: To protect its cables in the heat, the utility cuts voltage in your network. Machines heat slower and compressors run hot.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison voltage reduction announcements during heat waves
eventCatalog.realFrequency: August 2022: 8% in parts of Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx, about 252,000 customers. Another heat wave: 8% in parts of Brooklyn and Queens, 150,200 customers. June 2025: reduced voltage in Brooklyn and Staten Island, more than 168,000 customers asked to conserve.
eventCatalog.note: Heating power falls with the square of the voltage: 0.92 x 0.92 = 0.85, so boilers recover about 15% slower. The 5% loss of capacity at the rush, for the two or three days it lasts, is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: The machine was built for 240 volts
eventCatalog.text: The new espresso machine never quite keeps up at the rush. The electrician measures 208 volts at the outlet.

cause.when: the espresso machine was ordered without the roadmap step check_water_and_power in a building with a 208V supply

eventCatalog.realSignal: Voltage of the building supply against the rating plate of the machine
eventCatalog.realFrequency: 208V three-phase supply is common in commercial buildings; a 4,500W heater rated for 240V gives about 3,380W on 208V.
eventCatalog.note: A 25% loss of heating power: slower steam recovery when two baristas work. The fix is a 208V element: $380 + two hours at $250. The capacity loss is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Water main break
eventCatalog.text: The street is a river and your taps are dry. The city gives no hour for the repair.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DEP water main break reports; freeze-thaw weeks
eventCatalog.realFrequency: 552 breaks in fiscal 2025, the most since fiscal 2015: 7.9 per 100 miles of main (446, 459, 403 and 359 in the four years before). The first four months of fiscal 2026 ran 18% higher.
eventCatalog.note: Without water a food business cannot wash hands or dishes: closed until it returns. The one-day duration is my estimate. Afterwards the water may run brown: see brown_water_after_main_work. A cellar under the break floods; anything electrical down there is lost.

eventCatalog.name: Planned water shut-off
eventCatalog.text: Notices on the doors: no water tomorrow from 8 a.m. until the end of the workday.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Posted city shut-off notices for street work
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Notices are posted at least 24 hours ahead; one city project used a 72-hour advisory and a 24-hour confirmation.
eventCatalog.note: Half a day lost unless the owner shifts the hours. After the water returns, run the cold taps before reconnecting the filter.

eventCatalog.name: Low water pressure
eventCatalog.text: Open hydrants up and down the street pull the pressure down. The ice machine and the espresso machine fill slowly.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DEP notices about illegally opened hydrants during heat waves
eventCatalog.realFrequency: DEP issued a notice on hydrant use and water pressure during the 2026 heat wave.
eventCatalog.note: The 2% loss is my estimate. A softening cartridge has a maximum flow of 0.5 gallons a minute, so low pressure shows first at the filtered line.

eventCatalog.name: Gas shut off in the building
eventCatalog.text: A leak upstairs. The utility locks the gas for the whole building until the piping is repaired, inspected and pressure-tested.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison or National Grid gas shut-off tags; Buildings Department gas work permits at the address

effects.scope: shops with a gas water heater or gas oven

eventCatalog.realFrequency: New York restaurants have waited months: one in Chelsea more than seven months, one in Greenwich Village four months (2014); businesses in Riverdale were without gas from September 25, 2024 into December.
eventCatalog.note: The landlord must repair, the Buildings Department must certify the repair, then the utility tests the lines. A shop with a gas water heater has no hot water for the whole wait; the way out is an electric heater: $3,300 and about three days. An all-electric shop is not affected.

eventCatalog.name: Payment company outage
eventCatalog.text: The register cannot reach its servers. Cards fail or run offline; shops tape up cash-only signs.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Status page of the payment company
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Square: most of a day on September 7-8, 2023; one owner said he had never seen an outage longer than half an hour in five years, another counted almost $18,000 of lost business. Toast: a tracker counts 45 incidents in two years, 127 hours 31 minutes in all.
eventCatalog.note: 90% of orders are paid by card; if half of those customers walk away, 45% of a day is lost: 1.5% of the month. The walk-away share is my estimate. Offline mode keeps cards working when it is switched on in advance.

eventCatalog.name: A cloud outage freezes registers everywhere
eventCatalog.text: A failure at a cloud provider takes down ordering apps, loyalty programs and many registers at once.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Cloud provider status pages
eventCatalog.realFrequency: October 20, 2025: an Amazon Web Services outage left many restaurants on Toast with complete system failures. July 19, 2024: a faulty CrowdStrike update pushed businesses worldwide to cash only.
eventCatalog.note: Half a day with half the card customers lost. Owners told a newspaper that offline mode does not always work.

eventCatalog.name: Internet out on the block
eventCatalog.text: A cut fiber line. Wi-Fi is gone, the register is offline and online orders stop.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Provider outage maps; 311 reports
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Queens, 2017: vandals cut a Spectrum fiber line, 60,000 customers were out for more than 15 hours and card sales were impossible in some neighborhoods; one shop owner lost at least $500 of card sales. November 12, 2024: Verizon Fios out about four hours along the East Coast.
eventCatalog.note: With a cellular backup line: no loss. With offline mode only: cards still work, but laptop guests leave and delivery orders stop: 30% of the day is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Offline payments never arrive
eventCatalog.text: A barista logs out of the register to "fix" it before the internet returns. Every card payment taken offline that day is gone.

cause.when: cards were taken offline during an outage and the roadmap step plan_for_outages was skipped

eventCatalog.realSignal: Pending offline payments on the device
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Square: offline payments must upload within 72 hours of the start of the offline session; pending payments are lost if you log out, delete the app or reset the device; the seller is liable for declined, expired or disputed offline payments.
eventCatalog.note: Half a day of card sales: $1,700 x 90% x 50% = $765.

eventCatalog.name: The only card reader dies
eventCatalog.text: The register screen stays black. Until a replacement arrives you can take cash only, and by law you must keep taking it.

cause.when: the register passes 48 months with no second device

eventCatalog.realSignal: Age of the register; number of payment devices
eventCatalog.realFrequency: No failure statistic found; the IRS writes a register off over five years.
eventCatalog.note: A new Square Register is $899; two days of delivery is my estimate. With a second terminal nothing is lost.

eventCatalog.name: Break-ins on the block
eventCatalog.text: A crew is smashing glass doors before dawn and prying open registers. Four shops on one avenue in one night.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYPD precinct burglary pattern alerts
eventCatalog.realFrequency: March 2026, Maspeth: a crew hit four businesses in one early morning, smashed a bakery's glass front door and took $250 from the register. Williamsburg and Greenpoint: 10 business burglaries between February 22 and March 4, about $7,300 taken in all.
eventCatalog.note: A door pane is quoted at $400-$900 on general cost pages (no reliable New York price found); $650 + $250 of cash. A shop that leaves the drawer empty and open loses only the glass.

eventCatalog.name: Roaches move into the espresso machine
eventCatalog.text: Warm, damp and full of crumbs: the cabinet under the machine is the best address in the shop for a roach.

cause.when: pest_control is none for 3 months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Months without an exterminator visit
eventCatalog.realFrequency: A New Zealand technician finds cockroaches in about 10% of the commercial coffee machines he services. In May 2025 California inspectors closed a tonic bar after finding live roach nymphs in the cabinet under its espresso machine.
eventCatalog.note: Leads to this pack's pest_activity violation. One technician hour ($250) to open and clean the machine. The reputation loss is a game value.

eventCatalog.name: Below the roaster minimum
eventCatalog.text: The machine on your counter belongs to the roaster, and the contract says 30 lb a week. You are buying 18.

cause.when: the machine came through a roaster program and monthly orders fall below the minimum for 2 months

eventCatalog.realSignal: Pounds of coffee bought per week against the contract minimum
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Buying guides put typical minimums at 20-40 lb a week or $300-$600 of coffee a week. In Italy, where lending the machine is the norm, a court enforced a penalty on a bar that missed a 144 kg a month commitment.
eventCatalog.note: The 3% on cost of goods stands for paying for coffee you do not sell or a surcharge; contracts differ and none is published. At the reference 84 kg (185 lb) a month the shop buys about 43 lb a week: above a 30 lb minimum, below it if sales halve.

eventCatalog.name: A cafe nearby is selling everything
eventCatalog.text: A shop three blocks away closes this month. Its fridges, grinders and furniture go for a fraction of new.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Closures in the neighborhood; restaurant auction listings
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Dealers: buyers pay 30-70% less than new; the seller gets 10-30% of what the equipment cost.
eventCatalog.note: A positive event. The same numbers are what the player gets when he closes his own shop.

eventCatalog.name: Con Edison offers to pay for efficient equipment
eventCatalog.text: A contractor from the utility program offers a free look at your lighting and refrigeration. The program pays most of the upgrade.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison small business program funding (first come, first served)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: The program covers up to 70% of the cost of energy efficiency upgrades for customers under 300 kW; up to 100% in some Southeast Queens neighborhoods.
eventCatalog.note: Work started before the preliminary offer letter does not qualify. Refrigeration equipment must be UL listed or NSF certified.

eventCatalog.name: December: buy equipment before the year ends
eventCatalog.text: Equipment bought and switched on by December 31 can be deducted in full on this year's return.
eventCatalog.realSignal: IRS Section 179 limit for the tax year

effects.add: minus the cost of equipment placed in service this year

eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every year. 2026 limit: $2,560,000, reduced once purchases pass $4,090,000; 100% special depreciation applies to property acquired after January 19, 2025.
eventCatalog.note: For a cafe the limit never binds; the deduction cannot exceed the profit of the business.

mechanics.title: Equipment wears out, and neglect has a date
mechanics.playerDecision: Each month: the care levers (espresso_service, water_treatment, refrigeration_care, hvac_service). At purchase: new or used.
mechanics.engineMath: Every owned item keeps an age in months and a care record. With care, an item serves lifespanMonths and then must be replaced (or pays one average repair every 6 months). Without care it fails at lifespanNeglectedMonths, and specific neglect has its own clock (see extra.eventCatalog cause.when). A failure is not a dice roll: it fires in the month the clock runs out, with a repair cost, days of downtime and, for refrigeration, spoiled stock. The lifespanMonths field is in the pack today but the engine ignores it: nothing ever breaks.

mechanics.title: Four ways to get the machine
mechanics.playerDecision: For the espresso machine and the fridges: buy new, buy used, lease, or take the roaster's machine.
mechanics.engineMath: New: full price, full lifespan, 12-month warranty if installed by a certified technician. Used: about half price, half the life left, 0-3 months of warranty, and a hidden-scale failure unless inspected. Lease: no cash up front, a fixed payment for 60 months (principal x 0.0217 at 11%), 8.875% sales tax on each payment, and the debt survives the shop through the personal guarantee. Roaster program: no cash up front and service included, but a weekly minimum of coffee at the roaster's price; falling below the minimum for two months triggers roaster_minimum_shortfall. Selling: the player recovers 10-30% of what he paid.

mechanics.title: One machine, one grinder, one register: single points of failure
mechanics.playerDecision: Buy a spare (second grinder, batch brewer, second card terminal), pay for a service plan with a loaner, or accept the risk.
mechanics.engineMath: Sales lost = daily sales x share of orders that need the dead item x days down. Share: espresso machine or only grinder 65%, ice machine 50% of summer orders, register 45% (card customers who walk), hot water or water supply 100%. Days down: with a service plan 1 day; without 3 days; a failure on Saturday adds 2 days; a heat-wave month adds 2 days for refrigeration and air conditioning. A spare sets the share to zero for its item. Labor: $250 an hour with a one-hour minimum; emergency and weekend work at double the regular rate.

mechanics.title: Outages: the 2-hour rule, the 12-hour claim, the 72-hour law
mechanics.playerDecision: Before: thermometers or sensors, offline mode, cash float, backup line, insurance endorsements. After: discard or keep the stock (shortcut), notify the Health Department, file the claim.
mechanics.engineMath: An announced outage of H hours closes the shop for H hours. If H is more than 2, perishable stock ($600) is lost unless the player keeps it (shortcut keep_food_after_outage -> spoiled_food). If H is more than 12 and the cause is the utility's own equipment, a filed claim returns the stock up to $12,900; a storm returns nothing until 72 hours. Insurance: the spoilage endorsement pays the stock; utility interruption pays lost income after its waiting period. A card outage costs the card customers who walk unless offline mode was set up; an internet outage costs nothing with a backup line.

mechanics.title: A second-hand space comes with second-hand equipment
mechanics.playerDecision: Pay for an inspection before signing (roadmap step check_inherited_equipment) or find out later.
mechanics.engineMath: A former cafe or a bought business brings its air conditioner, water heater and sometimes fridges with an age the player does not see: age = a fixed share of lifespan set per place (for example 70%). The inspection step reveals the ages and lets the player price replacements into the deal. Without it, the first failure comes when the clock runs out: the water heater at 120 months, the air conditioner at 180. Most leases put repair and replacement of the unit that serves the space on the tenant.
